articles.headline: Public schools across Kentucky will see changes starting Wednesday
articles.image_alt: School bus outside a Kentucky school
articles.excerpt: Kentucky's Senate Bill 101 takes effect July 15, requiring districts to expel students in grades 6-12 for at least a year if they injure or attempt to injure school staff. The law answers teacher unions' calls to put educator safety first, mandating law enforcement reporting of assaults.

articles.headline: Detroit man charged in fatal shooting of custodian outside Chrysler Elementary School
articles.image_alt: Police photo related to school shooting case
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors charged Kevin Flagg, 43, with second-degree murder in the July 2 shooting of Devin Burns, a 25-year-old contracted custodian for Detroit Public Schools, killed in the Chrysler Elementary parking lot after a dispute escalated. Flagg returns to court July 20.

articles.headline: Fitzgerald Public Schools cancels summer classes, camp after threatening email
articles.excerpt: Fitzgerald Public Schools in Warren, Michigan canceled all summer classes and camp programming after district leaders received a threatening email targeting multiple school buildings. Officials suspended programs while working with law enforcement to assess the threat.

articles.headline: Now It's Student Attacks on Teachers: Are Our Schools Out of Control?
articles.excerpt: A national commentary surveys the string of recent student attacks on teachers, from a Maryland stabbing to a Montana classroom beating, and asks whether schools have lost the authority to protect the adults in the classroom as discipline structures erode.

articles.headline: California schools must follow new cellphone, bathroom and safety laws
articles.excerpt: New California laws taking effect this school year require districts to restrict student cellphone use and expand campus safety measures, including staff training requirements and broader background checks for school employees.

articles.headline: Lockdown lifted at Edinburg North High School after 'no credible threat' found following reports of a weapon on campus
articles.excerpt: Edinburg North High School in Texas locked down July 6 after a parent reported a possible weapon on campus. Officers searched the school and lifted the lockdown within 40 minutes after finding no credible threat, though staff and parents said the scare renewed safety concerns.

articles.headline: 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' will require all GA public schools to install mobile panic alert systems beginning July 1
articles.excerpt: Beginning July 1, Georgia's 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' requires every public school to deploy mobile panic-alert devices, putting an emergency button in the hands of every teacher and administrator and linking directly to first responders. It honors two victims of school violence.

articles.headline: Minnesota's anonymous school threat reporting system law begins July 1
articles.excerpt: A Minnesota law taking effect July 1 requires every public school district and charter school to provide an anonymous way to report threats via app, website, or hotline, giving students and staff a faster channel to flag danger to administrators before it escalates.

articles.headline: July 1: New Mississippi laws take effect today
articles.excerpt: Among the new Mississippi laws taking effect July 1: anyone 18 or younger who commits a crime with a firearm will now be automatically charged as an adult. Backers frame the tougher stance as a deterrent to the weapons increasingly turning up on and around school campuses.

articles.headline: New 2026 K-12 School Safety Trends Report, Based on More Than 346,000 Alerts, Shows How Schools Are Improving Response Times, Coordination, and Outcomes in Emergencies
articles.excerpt: A new report drawing on more than 346,000 wearable panic-button alerts finds 88% involved behavioral incidents such as physical altercations, and 94% of school staff say having a panic button makes them feel safer on campus. Alert use rose 31% year over year.

archive.headline: Former Montgomery County school worker accused of assaulting elementary school staff
archive.excerpt: A former Montgomery County Public Schools employee allegedly trespassed inside Glen Haven Elementary and assaulted staff members, prompting an hour-long lockdown. The suspect was arrested after a brief foot pursuit and faces trespassing and assault charges.

archive.headline: 2 teachers stabbed in assault involving student at Harford County elementary school
archive.excerpt: Two teachers were stabbed by a student during afternoon dismissal at Roye-Williams Elementary School in Havre de Grace, Maryland. Both were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries and have been released; the student was detained and no children were hurt.
